Test a robust DBA combination on the full pool, as the regime is seasonal_dominated and ranking unstable, so a DBA that iteratively removes worst models may help.
I want to test a trimmed‑mean strategy on the full pool to see if trimming the extreme forecasts improves performance in this seasonal‑dominated, robust‑combination scenario.
Test a robust weighted combination using the pooled_meta_model (w1) on the full pool to see if advanced meta‑weighting improves over inverse_error.
The series is seasonal_dominated with medium predictability; a softmax weight over a smaller correlated‑group pool might reduce over‑fitting.
Test a weighted combination on pool1 using inverse_error to see if a smaller, more diverse pool improves the robust seasonal signal.
Test a robust median combination on the full pool to see if the median gives better robustness given high correlation groups.
Test a trimmed mean over the smaller, diverse pool1 to see if removing extremes improves robustness given high correlation groups.
Test a weighted softmax‑negative‑error combination on the full pool to see if a sharper weight allocation improves robustness in this seasonal‑dominated, stationary series.
Test a weighted combination using the “error_trend” weight method on the full pool to see if incorporating error dynamics improves performance under the seasonal_dominated regime.
Test a weighted combination on pool2 with inverse_error weights to see if a smaller, diversified pool improves robustness under the seasonal_dominated regime.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted weighted by w6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9928. Series context: trend strength 0.0 and seasonal strength 0.8199; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.01); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.972.
